<!-- plain-summary -->
This step runs the correctness test on a real multi-machine cluster while deliberately injecting failures — cutting the network between nodes, skewing clocks, and freezing processes. Storage bugs that lose or corrupt data almost always stay hidden until something breaks, so the guarantees are only trustworthy if they hold up while the system is under active disruption.

**Slice 4 of #329.** The fault injection the checked workload runs under — reusing M4.6's cluster and nemesis rather than building a second one.

**Scope:**
- Reuse #257's real multi-node M4 cluster (deploy/, #256) and its `tc netem` / `iptables` partition + `libfaketime` clock-skew + process-pause nemesis, driven across the **commit + repair path**.
- Include the live-node network-partition upgrade (#399), stronger than the `docker pause` freeze the Option-B leg uses.
- The clock-skew nemesis interacts with ADR-0024 clock-trust and the checker's real-time order — account for it explicitly.

**Depends on:** #257 (M4.6 cluster + nemesis), #256 (deploy/). **Refs:** #329, ADR-0041, ADR-0024, #399.

milestone.title: M4 — Production metadata backend
milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.

title: M329.4 — partition/skew/pause nemesis over the M4 cluster (reuse #257)
